description.value: Dosanko is a Japanese yoshoku restaurant in Vancouver's historic Japantown, founded by chef Nathan Lowey and his Hokkaido-born partner Akiyo Lowey, serving Western-influenced Japanese home cooking rooted in seasonal, locally sourced, and housemade ingredients. The kitchen follows a mottainai (no-waste) philosophy, crafting miso, shoyu, and dashi from scratch in-house. The cozy 45-seat dining room sits near Canada's oldest Japanese language school and is also available for private events up to 55 guests.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content is fully available and corroborates OSM address (566 Powell St), phone ((604)251-2020), and restaurant category. The navigation menu includes a 'Take out/Dine in' link confirming takeout service, and the menu page marks several items as (v) vegetarian and (vg) likely vegan. The COVID safety plan mentions washrooms being sanitized before every service, confirming on-site washrooms. No bike-specific amenities are mentioned anywhere on the site. A minor discrepancy exists between OSM opening hours (Tuesday–Saturday) and the website contact page (Wednesday–Saturday).
concerns: OSM opening_hours tag lists Tuesday–Saturday service, but the website contact page shows Wednesday–Saturday hours; OSM may be outdated.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operating restaurant with an active website, confirmed address, and takeout service — clearly useful to touring cyclists passing through Vancouver's Japantown.

Washrooms.detail: COVID safety plan states 'Washrooms sanitized before every service' and mentions sanitizer in both washrooms, confirming on-site customer washrooms

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Menu marks items with (v) for vegetarian (e.g. 'Crispy Cheesy (v)', 'Cheese Toast Combo v', 'Onigiri Combo (v)') and (vg) for likely vegan (e.g. 'Kimpira (vg) burdock and carrot with sweet soy sauce'). No GF labelling observed
